look_here_first: Compare the collar/ligule and mature awned spikelets with S. nutans, then check the whole plant. S. elliottii is the slender eastern sandy-woodland Indiangrass comparison; S. nutans is generally more robust with a conspicuous ligule and dense golden panicle. Habitat alone cannot confirm either species.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Reviewed draft finds eastern Texas records (e.g. Anderson and San Jacinto), but no verified project target-zone counties.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer project native status from statewide Texas nativity or transfer S. nutans county records.

best_field_traits: Slender growth form relative to typical robust S. nutans
Awned reproductive spikelets; examine at maturity
Inspect collar/ligule and spikelet hairs rather than relying on flower color
Often associated with eastern sandy open woodland; habitat is only supporting context
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Verify mature spikelet/ligule structure before distinguishing from S. nutans; the draft supports slender habit and eastern sandy-woodland association, not a fully measured diagnostic key.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. nutans is typically the robust tallgrass prairie Indiangrass with a conspicuous stiff membranous ligule/auricle-like collar and dense golden-bronze awned panicle. S. elliottii is generally slender and more associated with eastern sandy woodlands. Verify reproductive structures for confident ID; habit and habitat alone are insufficient.
